messages:
sam: noticed an uptick in GPU pod Pending + eviction churn in us-central1 around 02:14 UTC. pods show Pending with 'Insufficient GPUs' despite nodes reporting free GPUs a moment earlier.

nora: saw it too. eviction spikes from 02:15-02:28, ~4x baseline. cluster autoscaler didn't add capacity. any infra events?

raj: not seeing cloud-provider failures. but scheduler logs show a few 'assigning pod X to node Y' immediately followed by kubelet lease RPC errors: 

raj: ```
    scheduler: INFO assigned gpu-pod-abc -> us-central1-b-node-11
    kubelet[pid]: ERROR lease rpc failed: context deadline exceeded
    kubelet[pid]: INFO reclaimed device 0 for pod gpu-pod-abc
    kube-scheduler: WARN double-claim detected for pod gpu-pod-abc (node-11 vs node-27)
    ```

kevin: double-claim patterns suggest the scheduler's view and kubelet's device-plugin state are diverging during transient control-plane latency. When the scheduler times out waiting for device allocation ack it reassigns.

sam: sounds similar to ghost-slot behavior but with a clear control-plane timing window. proposal: implement a small 'allocation-grace' in scheduler that waits an extra 4s for device plugin annotations before rescheduling, and add a short ephemeral taint on nodes that report lease errors to avoid immediate reschedule.

nora: two tradeoffs: waiting increases end-to-end Pending time for some pods during real node failures; tainting reduces churn but may increase fragmentation if nodes are effectively healthy but slow.

raj: alternative quick mitigation: bump warm-pool in us-central1 by 6 nodes (estimated +$3.1k/day) for 90m and cordon nodes that hit lease error >3 times in 2m. That buys headroom while we test scheduler-grace change.

kevin: I can roll a scheduler canary (patch adds 4s allocation-grace and a histogram metric) to 10% of API masters. will need a config flip in feature flags.

ops-bot: autoscaler: us-central1 GPU warm-pool currently 8 nodes, free capacity 1. Recent events: scale-up +2 at 02:12 UTC.

sam: if canary looks good, we can make the allocation-grace permanent and add a follow-up to tune descheduler to avoid long-lived fragmentation caused by ephemeral taints.

nora: i've prepared a checklist: 1) start scheduler canary -> 10% masters, 2) cordon noisy nodes with `kubectl cordon --selector=leaseErrors>2` (ops will run), 3) monitor evictions and pod Pending latency.

raj: doing the cordon now for nodes that reported >2 lease errors in last 5m. will also annotate them with `infra/lease-noise=true` so we can trace in descheduler.

kevin: canary deployed. metric 'scheduler_allocation_grace_latency' visible on dashboard.

ops-bot: deploybot: scheduler canary deployed to masters: 10% (us-central1).

nora: 20m update: eviction rate down ~72%, Pending latencies improved by ~30%. cordoned nodes not causing customer impact.

sam: good. we should capture a post-incident note: root cause likely control-plane RPC jitter + aggressive scheduler reassignment. next steps: 1) make allocation-grace configurable (default 4s), 2) add ephemeral taint/cordon automation for noisy nodes, 3) run an offline sim for long-term fragmentation impact.

raj: will file follow-ups: INFRA-3482 (scheduler param), INFRA-3483 (ephemeral taint automation), DESCHED-900 (fragmentation sim).

kevin: lock: do not increase warm-pool unless eviction rate rises >5/min for 10m. cost hit otherwise.

ops-bot: alert cleared: gpu-eviction-count returned to baseline.

sam: closing thread. will post a short incident blurb in #postmortems and link follow-up tickets. :thumbsup:
